one_sentence_story: Hide your real hand behind a board and brush a rubber hand at the same speed. In one minute, your brain claims that fake hand as yours.
so_what_for_you: Your brain updates your body map every minute from sight and touch. That helps stroke care and makes tools feel like part of your arm.

jargon_map.plain: Feeling brush taps inside a fake hand when it is stroked in sync with your hidden real hand.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a puppet show tricking you into hearing the doll speak.

jargon_map.plain: Shut your eyes and point to your hand. Your finger lands two centimeters closer to the fake hand.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a compass needle pulled off path by a magnet.

jargon_map.plain: Brushing the two hands half a second apart so the brain spots the trick right away.
jargon_map.analogy: Like bad lip sync spoiling a film scene.

jargon_map.plain: A front brain strip that blends sight, touch, and joints to mark what is yours.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a guard checking two badges at the door.
